title: lucas-wu-all-hands-september-2026-talking-points-draft
content:
All-hands Sept 2026 - Lucas Wu (draft)

Purpose: quick update on product roadmap, Dedicated launch progress, Private pilot wins, ops & hiring. High-level narrative: steady growth, investing in reliability and enterprise readiness, focus on making inference cheaper and more predictable.

Agenda (5-7 min each section)
- Intro + company health (Lucas) - 5m
- Product roadmap highlights + Dedicated launch status (Product lead) - 7m
- Private deployments & customer stories (Solutions) - 6m
- Observability and Optimize updates (Eng) - 5m
- Hiring and org updates (People) - 4m
- Q&A - 15m

Key talking points
1) Company health
- ARR growth: on track vs Q2 plan (high level number TBD)
- Usage trends: Hosted API traffic +18% mo/mo; Dedicated commit renewals up
- Financial discipline: hitting unit-economics targets via Optimize suggestions

2) Product roadmap (3 bullets)
- Dedicated GA: rollout schedule, topline performance metrics vs baseline, customer feedback. Emphasize SLA commitments and predictable throughput.
- Private pilot traction: 3 pilots in regulated verticals (fintech, healthcare) - anonymized wins + next steps.
- Developer experience: streaming + function calling improvements shipped; upcoming SDK telemetry that will surface per-route costs.

3) Reliability & observability
- SRE improvements: latency p95 down 12% across common models; automatic fallback policies reduced incident blast radius.
- New tracing hooks in Console - early access for 2 pilot customers.

4) Cost/performance tooling (Optimize)
- Batch/caching recommendations saved X% tokens for early customers (share anecdata)
- Next: model quantization suggestions integrated into Console via profiles.

5) Hiring & org
- New hires: two infra engineers joining SRE, one Product Manager for Private.
- Open roles & how to refer - brief call to action.

Things to call out (tone: candid, product-first, pragmatic)
- We're prioritizing enterprise readiness - investments may slow some feature velocity but improve reliability and sales
- We are measuring everything - experiments tied to clear unit-econ goals
- Encourage engineers to file short postmortems / blameless notes when incidents happen

Q&A prep (anticipated Qs + suggested answers)
Q: How is Dedicated different from Hosted? (short)
A: Dedicated offers reserved GPU pools, SLA-backed latency/uptime, and data isolation. Hosted is for self-serve usage; Dedicated is for customers needing predictable throughput and contractual SLAs.

Q: Any concerns about capacity/cost with bigger models? (short)
A: We're investing in continual batching, KV caching, and model quantization profiles. For large models we recommend Dedicated or Private with tailored quantization to balance cost and latency.

Q: Timeline for Private GA? (short)
A: Private is in controlled pilot with 3 customers; GA depends on pilot feedback and security validation - aiming for H1 2027 (tentative).

Q: Will Optimize recommendations change default behavior? (short)
A: Defaults won't change automatically; Optimize will provide safe suggestions and admins can opt-in per workload.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self)
- Fill in ARR and concrete metrics before final draft
- Confirm which product lead will present roadmap (cc: Maya)
- Get 1-2 customer quotes from Solutions for Private pilots
- Add slide showing p95 latency improvement chart (ask Observability team)

Presentation notes for delivery
- Keep tone upbeat and practical; avoid jargon where possible
- Call attention to wins but acknowledge tradeoffs
- End with clear ask: referrals to open roles + invite for feedback via short survey link

Logistics
- Date/time: Sept 2, 2026 10:00 PT (confirm)
- Venue: all-hands Zoom + recording
- Slide owner: Lucas (finalize v0 by Aug 28)

Scratchpad / Alternate phrasings
- "We measure impact - not just features" -> use as a headline for culture slide
- For Dedicated: "predictable throughput, contractual SLAs, and predictable unit economics"

Notes: rough; will iterate once Maya and Samira add product numbers and customer quotes.
